questions.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $A(5,-3,1)$ and is parallel to the lines $r=⟨8,1,0⟩+s⟨3,2,5⟩$ and $r=⟨6,-5,10⟩+t⟨0,6,2⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
The direction vectors of the lines are ${v}_{1}=⟨3,2,5⟩$ and ${v}_{2}=⟨0,6,2⟩$, respectively. These vectors are parallel to the plane but not to each other.

We also know that the point $A(5,-3,1)$ lies on the plane and its position vector is $a=⟨5,-3,1⟩.$  

So, the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =a+s{v}_{1}+t{v}_{2} \\ r & =⟨5,-3,1⟩+s⟨3,2,5⟩+t⟨0,6,2⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find a normal vector to the plane

$$
r=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ -1 \\ 13\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,t,\,s\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
questions.worked_solution:
From the parametric equation, we have that $v=⟨0,-1,3⟩$ and $w=⟨1,2,-1⟩$ are parallel to the plane.

Now, we need to find a normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of $v$ and $w$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-5i+3j+k \\  & =⟨-5,3,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨-5,3,1⟩.$
